newsitem.title: USA: Orange County sheriff evaluates Citron for program.
newsitem.headline: Orange County sheriff evaluates Citron for program.

text.p: The Orange County, Calif., sheriff's department has begun evaluating former county Treasurer Robert Citron for a community work program that could keep him out of jail, his attorney said Tuesday.

Citron attorney David Wiechert said the sheriff's department would decide as early as Thursday whether Citron qualifies for the community work program in lieu of serving time in jail for his role in the county bankruptcy crisis.
Citron reported for processing Monday ahead of his official Friday booking date in order to begin his evaluation for community work, Wiechert said.
If Citron qualifies for the program, he would be given a work assignment instead of serving a year in county jail.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on December 6, 1994 after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy in June.
In November, a judge ordered Citron to spend a year in jail and pay a $100,000 fine for his role in the investment crisis. Citron was ordered to report to jail this Friday.
Citron pleaded guilty in April 1995 to six felonies, including counts of making untrue statements in the sale of securities and misusing public funds.
